## Summary

`rebar claim` records **no assignee** on the deployed MCP server instead of the configured
`ticket.default_assignee`. `_config_default_assignee` infers the config root as the TRACKER'S
PARENT directory — an assumption that holds only when the tracker lives inside the repo.

    # src/rebar/_commands/claim.py:84
    return config.compose_config(root=os.path.dirname(tracker)).ticket.default_assignee or ""

In a checkout the tracker is `<repo>/.tickets-tracker`, so the parent IS the repo root and
`rebar.toml` is found. The MCP server sets `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR=/var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets`,
whose parent `/var/gerrit/site` contains no `rebar.toml`. The lookup returns `""`, and the claim
records an empty assignee.

The `except Exception: return ""` guard ("a malformed config must never break a claim") means
this degrades **silently** — no warning, no error, just a ticket with no owner.

## Proven on the live box (2026-08-26, container `compose-mcp-1`)

Same call, two roots:

    CWD = /app
    compose_config(root=None)                    -> 'joeoakhart@navapbc.com'
    compose_config(root=dirname(REBAR_TRACKER_DIR)) -> ''
    tracker_dir(None)                            -> /var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets

    $ ls /var/gerrit/site/rebar.toml   -> No such file or directory
    $ ls /app/rebar.toml               -> 14163 bytes
    $ echo $REBAR_DEFAULT_ASSIGNEE     -> <unset>   (env override does not rescue it)

The env-override path (`REBAR_DEFAULT_ASSIGNEE`, `_config_sources.py:316`) is not set in the mcp
compose service, so nothing masks the bad root.

## Why this is the only site

`compose_config(root=os.path.dirname(` appears exactly once in `src/rebar` — this line. Every
other caller passes a real `repo_root` (`_engine_support/gates.py:154`, `reads.py:118,186,347`,
`verify_opcert.py:117`). `claim.py` is the outlier, and its own docstring asserts the
assumption it violates: "Read from the repo root (the tracker's parent)".

The MCP write path supplies no `repo_root` at all (`_mcp_writes.py` has no such reference), so
`repo_root` is `None` there — and `compose_config(root=None)` resolves correctly from CWD `/app`.
That is what makes the fix a deletion rather than an addition.

## Fix

Resolve config the way every other caller does — pass `repo_root` through (including `None`)
instead of substituting the tracker's parent:

    def _config_default_assignee(repo_root=None) -> str:
        try:
            return config.compose_config(root=repo_root).ticket.default_assignee or ""
        except Exception:
            return ""

`repo_root` is already in scope at the call site (`claim.py:175`, same function that computes
`tracker = config.tracker_dir(repo_root)` at `:154`). In a checkout this resolves the same
`rebar.toml` as today, so CLI behaviour is unchanged; on the box it finds `/app/rebar.toml`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A claim whose tracker sits OUTSIDE the repo resolves `ticket.default_assignee` from the
      repo root, not from the tracker's parent.
      Proof: `test_default_assignee_resolves_when_the_tracker_lives_outside_the_repo`
- [x] A claim in an ordinary checkout resolves the same value it does today — no behaviour
      change. Proof: the seven pre-existing tests in `test_claim_default_assignee.py` pass
      unmodified.
- [x] An explicit `--assignee` still wins over the default, and an explicit `--assignee ""`
      still clears it. Proof: `test_explicit_assignee_wins_over_default`,
      `test_explicit_empty_clears_no_fallback`
- [x] Regression coverage fails if the root reverts to `os.path.dirname(tracker)`.
      Proof: mutation-checked — restoring the old root turns the new test RED.
- [x] The PLAN-REVIEW GATE also resolves its config root correctly on a relocated store.
      Added after code review found the same root inference feeding
      `plan_review_precheck` / `_plan_review_gate_applies`: for a gate flag an empty config
      reads as OFF, so the start-work gate silently STOPPED APPLYING on the deployed server.
      Proof: `test_plan_review_gate_still_applies_when_the_tracker_lives_outside_the_repo`;
      restoring the old root produces `DID NOT RAISE`.


## Verification

    .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/ -k "default_assignee or claim_assignee" -q -p no:randomly
